en.name: Agnes of Rome
en.summary: Twelve-year-old Roman martyr whose refusal to renounce her faith made her one of the most venerated virgin saints.
en.body: Agnes was a girl of a noble Roman family, said to have been only twelve or thirteen years old when she was martyred during the persecution of Diocletian around 304. According to tradition, she had consecrated herself to Christ and refused marriage, and when a spurned suitor reported her Christian faith to the authorities, she was condemned to death and executed, reportedly by the sword, after other punishments failed to break her resolve. Her name became linked by wordplay to the Latin agnus, lamb, and it is customary for two lambs to be blessed on her feast day, their wool later woven into the pallium vestments given to archbishops. She is one of the seven women, besides Mary, named in the Roman Canon of the Mass.
